jobs.title: Development Director, School Engagement
jobs.description:
Overview

Since our founding in 1924, we've cut cardiovascular disease deaths in half, but there is still so much more to do. To overcome today’s biggest health challenges and accelerate this progress, we need passionate individuals like you. Join our movement, be part of the progress, and help ensure a healthier future for all. You matter, and so does the impact you can make with us.

We are currently hiring a Development Director, School Engagement. This is a full time, field-based position that requires extensive travel across the Los Angeles, East Los Angeles, and San Gabriel Valley areas. Flexibility in working hours, including early mornings and evenings, is essential to accommodate the needs of schools and events.

In this fast-paced fundraising/sales position, you will engage K-12 students with the Kids Heart Challenge and American Heart Challenge, working with hundreds of schools to promote physical activity and learning. The role also involves extensive data management, continuously updating account information in our customer relationship management (CRM) databases and Microsoft Office products.

Combine your love for fundraising and sales with your passion for kids' health!
The American Heart Association's Kids Heart Challenge
is all about equipping kids with ways to keep their hearts and brains healthy and raising funds for the health of all hearts. Meet one of our heart heroes here and learn more!

The Association offers many resources to help you maintain work-life harmonization through your changing needs and life situations. To help you be successful, you will have access to Heart U, our award-winning corporate university, as well as additional training and support, locally.

\#TheAHALife is more than a company culture; it is our way of life. It embodies our commitment to work-life harmonization and is guided by our core values where our employees can thrive both personally and professionally. Discover why you will Be Seen. Be Heard. Be Valued at the American Heart Association by following us on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, and at heart.jobs.

Responsibilities

This position is directly responsible for meeting an overall fundraising goal (participant income and corporate sponsorship) through exceptional volunteer recruitment and engagement, customer service and account management - all while motivating kids to take their health to heart
.

Recruit and engage students through schools and districts in life-saving initiatives including Kids Heart Challenge and American Heart Challenge programs.
Implement strategies and initiatives to fully engage students through classroom challenges, activities and student assemblies (in-person and digital experiences).
Develop and cultivate relationships on an ongoing basis with teachers, principals and district superintendents.
Establish and maintain outstanding customer service with volunteers and other collaborators. This includes detailed planning and kick-off meetings to set schools up for success.
Manage and continuously update account information within our customer relationship management (CRM) databases and Microsoft products.
High volume account management that regularly involves working with 5-10 schools each day - in-person where possible or online/by phone.

Qualifications

3 years of relevant experience in fundraising, sales, or other related experience.
Ability to do daily local travel; requires access to reliable transportation at all times on an immediate basis.
University/College degree or equivalent experience.
Ability to work productively and efficiently from a home office and in the field consistent with the Association's flexible work arrangements policy.
Demonstrated ability to work independently and communicate proactively.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, "we can do this" environment.
This position demands extensive data management, requiring the continuous updating of account information within our CRM databases; Proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to efficiently manage and report on data using CRMs are essential.
Ability to lift and/or move large objects (such as boxes) with the expectation that heavier items would be broken down into smaller components or requesting additional assistance may be required before lifting and/or moving.
Candidates must be willing to work flexible hours, including early mornings and evenings, to effectively engage with schools and manage events.

Here are some of the preferred skills we are looking for:

Experience managing and cultivating volunteer relationships.
Knowledge of corporate and community networks.

Compensation & Benefits

Expected pay range will be $70,725 to $83,000 annually. Pay is commensurate with experience; geographic differentials to the pay range may apply. The American Heart Association reserves the right to pay more or less than the posted range.

The American Heart Association invests in its people. Here are the main components of our total rewards package. Visit Rewards & Benefits to see more details.

Compensation – Our goal is to ensure you have a competitive base salary. That’s why we regularly review the market value of jobs and make adjustments, as needed.
Performance and Recognition – You are rewarded for achieving success through annual salary planning and incentive programs; this position is incentive eligible based on achieving certain targets.
Benefits – We offer a wide array of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance, along with a robust retirement program that includes an employer match and automatic contribution. As a mark of our commitment to employee well-being, we also offer an employee assistance program, employee wellness program and telemedicine, and medical consultation.
Professional Development – You can join one of our many Employee Resource Groups (ERG) or be a mentor/mentee in our professional mentoring program. Heart U is the Association’s national online university, with more than 100,000 resources designed to meet your needs and busy schedule.
Work-Life Harmonization – The Association offers Paid Time Off (PTO) at a minimum of 16 days per year for new employees. The number of days will increase based on seniority level. You will also have a total of 12 paid holidays off each year, which includes several days off at the end of the year.
Tuition Assistance - We support the career development of all employees. This program provides financial assistance to employees who wish to further their education and career in relation to their current duties and responsibilities, or for potential future positions in the organization.

The American Heart Association’s 2028 Goal: Building on over 100 years of trusted leadership in cardiovascular and brain health, by 2028 the Association will drive breakthroughs and implement proven solutions in science, policy, and care for healthier people and communities. The greatest discoveries in health must reach everyone where they are.

At American Heart Association | American Stroke Association, our mission is to be a relentless force for a world of longer, healthier lives, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, religion, age, language, sexual orientation, national origin and physical or cognitive abilities.

Executive Director

Bishop & Company
is seeking an experienced Executive Director
on behalf of the Hawaii Parkinson Association
, a statewide nonprofit dedicated to helping Hawaii's community live well with Parkinson's Disease.

Why This Role

Strong nonprofits are built on strong leadership. - That's where you come in.

This is an opportunity to lead a respected Hawaii nonprofit and make a meaningful impact in the lives of individuals and families affected by Parkinson's Disease. As Executive Director, you will serve as the face of the organization, build community partnerships, drive fundraising efforts, and work closely with the Board of Directors to advance HPA's mission throughout the state.

What You'll Enjoy

Opportunity to lead a well-established statewide nonprofit organization
Meaningful, mission-driven work serving Hawaii's Parkinson's community
High-visibility leadership role with community impact
Partnership with an engaged Board of Directors and volunteer leaders
Ability to shape organizational growth and strategy
Comprehensive benefits package and bonus opportunity based on performance goals

Position Summary

The Executive Director provides strategic and operational leadership for the Hawaii Parkinson Association and serves as its primary ambassador, fundraiser, and community representative. This role is responsible for fundraising, donor relations, community outreach, volunteer engagement, strategic planning, and overall organizational management.

Key Responsibilities

Lead fundraising, donor cultivation, and stewardship efforts
Develop and execute organizational strategies and annual goals
Partner closely with the Board of Directors on planning and governance initiatives
Manage the organization's budget and financial performance
Build relationships with community, healthcare, corporate, and nonprofit partners
Serve as HPA's primary spokesperson and community representative
Lead volunteer recruitment, engagement, and development efforts
Oversee programs, events, and initiatives that support HPA's mission and growth

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree required
Five or more years of fundraising experience, preferably within a nonprofit organization, or equivalent leadership experience
Demonstrated success in fundraising, donor relations, corporate partnerships, and community engagement
Experience with strategic planning, budgeting, and volunteer leadership
Strong communication, relationship-building, and leadership skills
Ability to lead fundraising initiatives and cultivate key partnerships
Knowledge of Parkinson's Disease or related communities is a plus

Location:
Must reside in Hawaii; interisland and occasional mainland travel required.

Full-time with flexibility to attend community and fundraising events.

jobs.title: Deputy Director of Administration
jobs.description:
You are the senior strategic leader responsible for the vision, effectiveness, and long-term direction of the organizational support team, including Operations, Finance, and People & Culture. Partnering with the Executive Director, Senior Leadership Team, and Leadership Team, you strengthen the systems, resources, culture, and organizational capacity needed to achieve the agency's mission, vision, values, and strategic priorities. You lead through Directors and other agency leaders, creating clarity, accountability, and collaboration across functions while ensuring infrastructure is integrated, responsive, compliant, and positioned for sustainable growth. This position carries primary accountability for the administrative health of the agency, exercising delegated authority during the Executive Director's absence. You lead by example, modeling and driving a culture of accountability and support, and lead in shaping a workplace where people feel valued, supported, and inspired to do their best work. 

This position supervises the Organizational Support Team leadership, currently including the Director of Finance, Director of Operations, and Director of People & Culture. The Deputy Directors jointly support cross-organizational alignment, leadership effectiveness, delivery of agency strategy, and organizational success and sustainability while maintaining primary accountability for their respective portfolios. 

Strategic Leadership & Organizational Capacity  
Drive the vision, strategy, and long-term priorities for the Organizational Support Team, ensuring alignment with the agency’s mission, vision, values, and strategic plan. 
Partner with the Executive Director and Senior Leadership Team to translate organizational priorities into clear administrative, financial, operational, and workforce goals.  
Anticipate organizational needs and strengthen the capacity, structures, systems, and resources necessary to achieve the agency’s current and future priorities. 
Serve as a senior leader in organizational effectiveness, readiness, sustainability, and the continuous development of TPN's internal infrastructure. 
Lead Organizational Support functional team and participate in Functional Lead meetings to lead and drive agency strategic priorities. 
Co-lead Leadership Team meetings alongside the Deputy Director of Programs and help ensure coordinated effort across the agency. 
Represent the Executive Director in internal and external forums when delegated and speak for the agency's administrative and operational commitments. 
Serve as the Executive Director's principal thought partner and confidential advisor. 

Organizational Stewardship & Systems Integration  
Provide strategic leadership and oversight of Operations, Finance, and People & Culture, ensuring these functions are aligned, integrated, and positioned to support the agency’s mission. 
Strengthen organizational infrastructure, systems, and processes to promote effectiveness, sustainability, innovation, and continuous improvement. 
Ensure Directors have clear accountability for functional strategy, day-to-day management, performance, staffing, and results within their areas of responsibility. 
Promote and ensure intra and interdepartmental collaboration, systems integration, and coordinated solution generation to ensure delivery of functional department and agency goals. 
Identify cross-functional gaps, duplication, or inefficiencies and lead improvements that make organizational systems easier to navigate, more responsive, and more effective. 

Financial, Operational & Risk Stewardship  
Partner with the Director of Finance and Executive Director to align financial planning, resource allocation, and organizational priorities. 
Ensure financial strategy, forecasting, daily operations, and decision-making support organizational sustainability, growth, and mission impact. 
Provide strategic oversight of organizational risk, compliance, internal controls, administrative policies, and operational readiness in partnership with functional Directors and the Executive Director. 
Ensure Operations systems and infrastructure effectively support staff, programs, facilities, technology, safety, continuity, and changing organizational needs. 
Use organizational and financial data to identify risks, trends, capacity needs, and opportunities for greater efficiency and effectiveness, and ensure appropriate mitigation or improvement plans are implemented. 
Hold and protect confidential information with consistent discretion. 
Ensure the Executive Director is briefed and decision-ready: surface emerging risks and opportunities early and directly. 

People & Organizational Culture  
Provide strategic leadership and oversight of workforce planning, organizational development, and employee experience in partnership with the Director of People & Culture. 
Promote a culture of accountability, collaboration, empowerment, and belonging that supports employee and organizational success. 
Develop and sustain leadership capacity and continuity, organizational readiness, and a strong internal talent bench to support continuity and future growth including intentional development pathways for staff with lived experience. 
Provide strategic direction for employee and leadership learning and development, ensuring workforce development priorities build capacity and align with organizational goals. 
Ensure people systems, policies, and practices are aligned with organizational values, equity commitments, legal requirements, and the agency's approach to shared leadership. 

Staff Support, Training, and Supervision  
Provide leadership, direction, and support to Directors within the Organizational Support Team. 
Directly supervise, develop, and evaluate Director-level staff, providing coaching, feedback, and support to strengthen leadership effectiveness. 
Support Directors in navigating complex organizational challenges, decision-making, and cross-functional priorities. 
Work to create and maintain a workforce reflective and responsive to the communities we serve. Prioritize lived experience and help sustain an agency culture that supports a diverse, representative, and stable workforce. 
Champion a culture of wellness, regulation, relational leadership, and accountability, including the agency's Creating Regulation and Resilience communication model. 

Senior Leadership  
Examine, develop, implement, document, and communicate the goals, priorities, and values of the agency. 
Provide strategic and visionary leadership for the agency in partnership with the Leadership Team. 
Prepare for, attend, and participate in leadership meetings and other meetings to work towards fulfilling agency mission, vision and values. 
Lead and serve on initiatives, temporary teams and work groups. 
Collaborate with agency staff and stakeholders to carry out the mission of TPN. 
Represent the agency positively and build relationships with stakeholders and the communities we serve. 
Model and drive a culture of accountability and support, in alignment with the Two Accountabilities.  
Support agency growth and sustainability and model the values and mission of TPN. 
Serve as the Executive Director's designated backup when delegated, supporting continuity of leadership and decision-making during periods of absence. 
Maintain a working knowledge of the agency's programs sufficient to speak credibly about TPN's participants, programs, and outcomes. 

Experience we are interested in:

Master's degree in business administration, nonprofit management, organizational leadership, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and significant relevant leadership experience. 
Six or more years of progressively responsible organizational, administrative, operational, financial, people, or nonprofit leadership experience. 
Six or more years of experience supervising a diverse team, including experience supervising and developing Director- and Manager-level leaders. 
Experience leading multiple departments or functional areas and implementing strategic initiatives from planning through implementation. 
Experience providing strategic oversight of finance, operations, people-related functions, organizational systems, or a combination of these areas. 
Experience with organizational planning, change management, process improvement, risk management, or organizational development. 
Experience working in nonprofit organizations and providing organizational leadership as part of an Executive or Senior Leadership Team. 
Experience partnering with a Board of Directors, including preparing and presenting materials to a board or board committee. 
Fluency with the systems a senior leader relies on to run an organization: financial and accounting systems, HRIS and payroll, case management or client data systems, board and project reporting tools, and the data analysis needed to interpret them. 
Ability to work independently with limited supervision while managing highly strategic, mission-critical work and priorities. 
Lived experience with the criminal legal system, incarceration, community supervision, and/or addiction and recovery is valued and strongly preferred, and is considered a meaningful qualification for this role alongside professional experience. 
Must possess a valid driver’s license and have access to a motor vehicle during work hours that is covered by adequate car insurance. 
Must complete a background check, employment verification, motor vehicle records check, and a drug screen that does not test for marijuana. Consistent with Oregon's ban-the-box law and TPN's values, conviction history is not requested until after an initial interview, is assessed individually against the duties of this position, and is not automatically disqualifying. Company Description
Operation Vets With Nets is a nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting military veterans through outdoor and recreational activities that promote connection, wellness, and community. The organization focuses on creating safe, inclusive, and supportive experiences that help veterans build relationships and improve quality of life. Programs are designed to reduce isolation, encourage peer support, and provide positive outlets through structured events and initiatives. Operation Vets With Nets collaborates with partners, volunteers, and donors to expand its impact and reach more veterans in need. The organization values integrity, service, and compassion in all aspects of its work.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Chief Operating Officer is a senior executive responsible for translating OVWN's mission, strategic direction, and organizational priorities into effective operations. The COO will oversee the organizational systems supporting OVWN's fishing programs, North Carolina Veteran House, Headquarters operations, and future Veteran House expansion. OVWN has a strong preference for candidates with significant senior military leadership and command experience.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

·        Direct and coordinate OVWN's day-to-day organizational operations.
·        Translate CEO and Board strategic priorities into actionable operating plans.
·        Oversee Headquarters operations and coordination with the North Carolina Veteran House.
·        Ensure both OVWN's fishing program and Veteran House programs receive appropriate organizational support.
·        Supervise assigned directors and senior managers.
·        Establish organizational policies, procedures, performance measures, and accountability systems.
·        Coordinate annual operating plans with Finance and program leadership.
·        Monitor staffing, contracts, expenditures, organizational performance, and resource requirements.
·        Establish standardized operating procedures for Veteran House operations.
·        Identify organizational and operational risks and recommend mitigation strategies.
·        Evaluate organizational processes and implement continuous improvements.
·        Support planning and implementation for future Veteran Houses.
·        Coordinate relationships among Headquarters, Veteran Houses, contractors, volunteers, community partners, and other stakeholders.
·        Provide operational assessments and recommendations to the CEO and Board.
·        Represent OVWN with senior military, veteran, government, corporate, nonprofit, and community leaders when required.
·        Promote a leadership culture based on integrity, accountability, teamwork, service, and responsible stewardship.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

·        Bachelor's degree in business administration, public administration, nonprofit management, operations management, organizational leadership, or related field.
·        At least seven years of progressively responsible executive or senior leadership experience.
·        Demonstrated experience leading personnel, budgets, programs, and complex operations.
·        Experience developing and implementing organizational strategy.
·        Strong decision-making, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
·        Exceptional written, verbal, and interpersonal communication abilities.
MILITARY / VETERAN LEADERSHIP PREFERENCE

OVWN strongly values military experience. Military experience complements, but does not replace, the technical, professional, educational, and leadership qualifications required for this position.
·        Retired General/Flag Officers are strongly encouraged to apply.
·        Retired O-6 officers with significant command experience are highly desirable.
·        Senior military leaders with experience managing complex organizations, personnel, budgets, facilities, and geographically dispersed operations are strongly preferred.
·        Senior enlisted leaders with significant command-level organizational leadership experience may also be considered when combined with appropriate executive qualifications.
·        Experience at General/Flag Officer, major command, combatant command, service headquarters, joint, or comparable senior organizational levels is highly desirable.
ADDITIONAL PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

·        Master's degree in business, public administration, strategic studies, organizational leadership, or related discipline.
·        Senior nonprofit or veteran-service leadership experience.
·        Experience developing multi-location organizations.
·        Experience working with Boards of Directors.
·        Experience establishing public-private partnerships.

ORGANIZATION-WIDE EXPECTATIONS

·        Place service to veterans and their families at the center of organizational decisions.
·        Demonstrate respect for veterans of every military branch, rank, occupational specialty, era, background, and service experience.
·        Recognize OVWN's fishing program as a core component of the organization's history and mission.
·        Support the integration of fishing programs and Veteran House initiatives.
·        Treat volunteer boat captains and other volunteers as essential mission partners.
·        Protect confidential and sensitive participant information.
·        Maintain appropriate professional boundaries and refer medical, behavioral-health, and clinical matters to appropriately credentialed professionals.
·        Demonstrate integrity, accountability, teamwork, service, and responsible stewardship.
·        Comply with OVWN policies, safety requirements, and applicable laws.

APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS

·        Current resume.
·        Cover letter describing relevant professional experience and interest in OVWN's mission.
·        Professional references upon request.
Veteran applicants are encouraged to describe relevant military leadership, command, staff, operational, technical, administrative, and program-management experience in terms applicable to the position. Selected candidates may be required to verify education, credentials, driving eligibility, or other job-related requirements consistent with applicable law.

company FutureSight location Chicago, United States (remote) work mode remote posted 1 Sept

### The Opportunity
FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead [Omnex](https://omnex-ecommerce.replit.app/), an AI-native operating system for multi-channel ecommerce sellers, currently in build at our studio. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.
Today's e-commerce businesses run on fragmented software and manual coordination. Sellers operating across Amazon, Shopify, eBay, Walmart, and other channels constantly switch between dashboards, reconcile conflicting data, and make hundreds of operational decisions every day across pricing, inventory, advertising, fulfillment, and customer support.
The opportunity sits within a global ecommerce market exceeding $1 trillion in annual GMV, where millions of sellers increasingly operate across multiple channels but lack any unified operational intelligence layer.
### Market Context
[Omnex](https://omnex-ecommerce.replit.app/) replaces this fragmented workflow with an autonomous, multi-agent AI workforce. Instead of giving sellers another dashboard, Omnex continuously understands the business, reasons across every sales channel, and proactively executes operational decisions—from optimizing pricing and inventory to managing advertising, forecasting demand, and coordinating customer support. Every AI agent shares the same business context, learns from outcomes, and works together to optimize the business as a whole.
### About FutureSight
FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.
You’ll co-create with a proven studio team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.
### The Partnership
Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception
Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding
Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one
Investor and advisor network across logistics, vertical AI, and early-stage capital markets
A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight's cross-functional team as your partner
### What you'll own
As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead its execution.
Strategy — Refine the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning
Customer Development — Lead pilots with ecommerce sellers, convert them to paid engagements, and build the go-to-market motion
Product — Partner with the FutureSight product and engineering team to ship V1 and iterate on user feedback
Capital — Lead the seed raise, supported by FutureSight's network and traction
Team — Recruit and lead the founding team, and establish the cultural foundation of the company
### Co-Founder Profile
Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company
Demonstrated success in B2B SaaS go-to-market, including sales and customer engagement
Fundraising fluency, with the ability to develop investor narratives and close capital
Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent
Clear-eyed understanding of the risks and demands of co-founding a venture-backed company
Direct experience in ecommerce — operated a multi-channel business, sold software into this market, or built tools for ecommerce sellers at scale
Network within the ecommerce seller community (Amazon sellers, Shopify operators, 3PL partners)
### How to Apply
Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.
FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

Rather than directing individual technology strategies or overseeing day-to-day program execution, the Managing Director influences outcomes through strategic leadership, governance, relationship building, facilitation, and consensus. The role connects executives, technology leaders, governance bodies, and industry partners to strengthen collaboration, drive innovation, and ensure participating associations achieve greater value together than they could independently.

What can we offer you?

GreenStone trusts the people we hire. We empower employees to make the best decisions for the customer and the company.

GreenStone has an outstanding Total Rewards package, which includes, but is not limited to:

15 vacation days, 12 sick days, and 12 paid holidays per year
401(k) plan – up to a 9% employer contribution/match

Paid Parental leave

$6,000 lifetime maximum Student Debt repayment program or tuition assistance

Our $16 billion portfolio of customers, ranging from rural homeowners to global agriculture and food businesses, provides our employees with a unique opportunity to maintain a local presence while working for a top workplace. Provide executive-level support and escalation guidance for major cross-association initiatives.
Help resolve issues involving strategy, funding, prioritization, governance, or stakeholder alignment.
Maintain organizational continuity and institutional knowledge across strategic initiatives.

Review shared technology budgets, forecasts, and investment proposals to assess business impact.
Advise leadership on technology investment decisions, cost drivers, and financial trade-offs.
Promote transparency, reduce duplication, and maximize the return on collaborative investments.
Partner with participating CEOs to continually enhance the effectiveness and value of the collaboration.

Leadership & Communication

Executive-level communication, presentation, and facilitation skills.
Proven ability to influence and build consensus across diverse stakeholder groups.
Strong relationship-building skills with executives, technology leaders, vendors, and industry partners.
Ability to navigate complex organizations and balance competing priorities.

Technical & Strategic Expertise

Deep knowledge of technology strategy, digital transformation, IT governance, and technology investment planning.
Expertise in multi-stakeholder governance and collaborative leadership models.
Strong understanding of technology trends and their business implications.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and modern business technologies.

Collaboration & Influence

Exceptional skills in facilitation, stakeholder engagement, and cross-functional leadership.
Demonstrated ability to lead through influence rather than direct authority.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.

Company Description
Operation Vets With Nets is a nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting military veterans through outdoor and recreational activities that promote connection, wellness, and community. The organization focuses on creating safe, inclusive, and supportive experiences that help veterans build relationships and improve quality of life. Programs are designed to reduce isolation, encourage peer support, and provide positive outlets through structured events and initiatives. Operation Vets With Nets collaborates with partners, volunteers, and donors to expand its impact and reach more veterans in need. The organization values integrity, service, and compassion in all aspects of its work.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Chief Operating Officer is a senior executive responsible for translating OVWN's mission, strategic direction, and organizational priorities into effective operations. The COO will oversee the organizational systems supporting OVWN's fishing programs, North Carolina Veteran House, Headquarters operations, and future Veteran House expansion. OVWN has a strong preference for candidates with significant senior military leadership and command experience.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

·        Direct and coordinate OVWN's day-to-day organizational operations.
·        Translate CEO and Board strategic priorities into actionable operating plans.
·        Oversee Headquarters operations and coordination with the North Carolina Veteran House.
·        Ensure both OVWN's fishing program and Veteran House programs receive appropriate organizational support.
·        Supervise assigned directors and senior managers.
·        Establish organizational policies, procedures, performance measures, and accountability systems.
·        Coordinate annual operating plans with Finance and program leadership.
·        Monitor staffing, contracts, expenditures, organizational performance, and resource requirements.
·        Establish standardized operating procedures for Veteran House operations.
·        Identify organizational and operational risks and recommend mitigation strategies.
·        Evaluate organizational processes and implement continuous improvements.
·        Support planning and implementation for future Veteran Houses.
·        Coordinate relationships among Headquarters, Veteran Houses, contractors, volunteers, community partners, and other stakeholders.
·        Provide operational assessments and recommendations to the CEO and Board.
·        Represent OVWN with senior military, veteran, government, corporate, nonprofit, and community leaders when required.
·        Promote a leadership culture based on integrity, accountability, teamwork, service, and responsible stewardship.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

·        Bachelor's degree in business administration, public administration, nonprofit management, operations management, organizational leadership, or related field.
·        At least seven years of progressively responsible executive or senior leadership experience.
·        Demonstrated experience leading personnel, budgets, programs, and complex operations.
·        Experience developing and implementing organizational strategy.
·        Strong decision-making, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
·        Exceptional written, verbal, and interpersonal communication abilities.
MILITARY / VETERAN LEADERSHIP PREFERENCE

OVWN strongly values military experience. Military experience complements, but does not replace, the technical, professional, educational, and leadership qualifications required for this position.
·        Retired General/Flag Officers are strongly encouraged to apply.
·        Retired O-6 officers with significant command experience are highly desirable.
·        Senior military leaders with experience managing complex organizations, personnel, budgets, facilities, and geographically dispersed operations are strongly preferred.
·        Senior enlisted leaders with significant command-level organizational leadership experience may also be considered when combined with appropriate executive qualifications.
·        Experience at General/Flag Officer, major command, combatant command, service headquarters, joint, or comparable senior organizational levels is highly desirable.

·        Master's degree in business, public administration, strategic studies, organizational leadership, or related discipline.

·        Experience establishing public-private partnerships.

### The Opportunity
FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead [Omnex](https://omnex-ecommerce.replit.app/), an AI-native operating system for multi-channel ecommerce sellers, currently in build at our studio. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.
Today's e-commerce businesses run on fragmented software and manual coordination. [Omnex](https://omnex-ecommerce.replit.app/) replaces this fragmented workflow with an autonomous, multi-agent AI workforce. FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

### The Partnership
Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception
Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding
Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one
Investor and advisor network across logistics, vertical AI, and early-stage capital markets
A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight's cross-functional team as your partner
### What you'll own
As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead its execution.
Strategy — Refine the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning
Customer Development — Lead pilots with ecommerce sellers, convert them to paid engagements, and build the go-to-market motion
Product — Partner with the FutureSight product and engineering team to ship V1 and iterate on user feedback
Capital — Lead the seed raise, supported by FutureSight's network and traction
Team — Recruit and lead the founding team, and establish the cultural foundation of the company
### Co-Founder Profile
Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company
Demonstrated success in B2B SaaS go-to-market, including sales and customer engagement
Fundraising fluency, with the ability to develop investor narratives and close capital
Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent
Clear-eyed understanding of the risks and demands of co-founding a venture-backed company
Direct experience in ecommerce — operated a multi-channel business, sold software into this market, or built tools for ecommerce sellers at scale
Network within the ecommerce seller community (Amazon sellers, Shopify operators, 3PL partners)

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.
FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

Overview

Executive Director
Lead With Purpose. Grow With Impact.

As an Executive Director (ED)
, you’ll play a pivotal role in leading an Aveanna branch and making a meaningful difference in the lives of patients, families, caregivers, and employees. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced leader who brings strong business acumen, exceptional communication skills, and a passion for delivering outstanding care and service.

As the leader of your branch, you’ll work closely with clinical, operations, and business development teams
to drive growth, strengthen relationships, support your team, and achieve exceptional patient care and financial outcomes.

Most importantly, you’ll be a trusted leader, mentor, and advocate
for your team and the families we serve.

What You’ll Do
Lead & Develop Your Team

Recruit, interview, and select highly qualified team members who share our commitment to exceptional service and care.
Provide coaching, mentorship, and ongoing professional development to help employees reach their full potential.
Ensure annual performance evaluations, goal setting, orientation, in-service training, and continuing education requirements are completed.
Build a positive, collaborative branch culture where employees feel supported, valued, and empowered to succeed.
Partner with supervisors and regional leadership to address opportunities and achieve branch goals.

Build Strong Patient & Community Relationships

Serve as a visible and engaged leader for patients, families, caregivers, referral sources, and employees.
Partner with branch and area leadership to create a welcoming and positive experience for new patients and families.
Support patient home visits and referral-source assessments as needed.
Monitor client satisfaction and take action to continuously improve the patient and family experience.
Collaborate with Business Development to build strong community relationships and develop strategic growth opportunities.

Drive Business & Operational Success

Develop and execute strategies that support sustainable branch growth.
Analyze financial statements, activity reports, and performance metrics to identify trends, opportunities, and areas for improvement.
Identify cost-saving opportunities and implement process improvements that enhance efficiency and quality.
Ensure accurate and timely completion of required reports and operational processes.
Monitor billing and collections to support strong financial performance and timely reimbursement.
Ensure the branch consistently follows applicable federal and state home care regulations, policies, and standards .

What You’ll Bring

Required

Associate degree or equivalent work experience in a related field.
2–3 years of management experience.
Ability to meet all applicable state requirements, including background checks and required work authorization.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-volume environment.
Strong leadership, organizational, relationship-building, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred

Four-year college degree.
Healthcare experience, particularly in pediatric home care , is a plus.

Why This Role Matters

The Executive Director is more than an operational leader—you’ll be the heart of the branch
, bringing people together around a shared commitment to quality care and exceptional service. You’ll have the opportunity to develop talented teams, strengthen relationships within your community, drive meaningful business growth, and help improve the lives of the patients and families we serve.

Physical & Environmental Requirements

This role requires the ability to:

Communicate effectively in English, both verbally and in writing.
Travel as needed.
Occasionally lift, carry, push, or pull up to 25 pounds.
Walk, stand, bend, kneel, reach, and twist for extended periods as needed.
Sit and climb stairs.
Meet required visual, hearing, and sensory acuity standards.
Work effectively in a variety of environments, including settings where exposure to allergens or other conditions may occur.

Additional Information

This job description is intended to provide an overview of the role and is not an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or activities. Responsibilities may change at any time based on business needs.

Vaccination Requirements

As an employer accepting Medicare and Medicaid funds, employees must comply with applicable health-related requirements in relevant jurisdictions, including required vaccinations and testing, subject to applicable medical or religious exemptions.

new_jobs.title: Associate Secretary JHM Board of Trustees & Advisor for Institutional Priorities (SOM - Office of the Dean/CEO)
new_jobs.description:
The Office of the Dean and CEO at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine is seeking an Associate Secretary JHM Board of Trustees & Advisor for Institutional Priorities.
The Associate Secretary serves as the principal board affairs liaison for the Johns Hopkins Medicine (JHM) Board of Trustees. Reporting to the Vice President/Chief of Staff in the Office of the Dean and CEO, this position serves as a strategic partner to the Dean/CEO, JHM Board Chair/Co-Chairs, and Vice President/Chief of Staff and provides leadership for board activities, trustee engagement related to JHM, board communications, and board operations.

The Associate Secretary works closely with the Johns Hopkins University (JHU) and Johns Hopkins Health System (JHHS) Board Offices to ensure alignment across the enterprise. This role combines strategic leadership, governance expertise, executive communications, and relationship management to support the Board's oversight of Johns Hopkins Medicine's mission, priorities, and long-term success.

About Johns Hopkins Medicine

The mission of Johns Hopkins Medicine is to improve the health of the community and the world by setting the standard of excellence in medical education, research and clinical care. Johns Hopkins Medicine (JHM) is an organizational construct that integrates the strategy and planning of the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine with the Johns Hopkins Health System. As one of the world's leading academic medical centers, JHM advances excellence in patient care, biomedical discovery, education, and community engagement.

The Johns Hopkins Medicine Board of Trustees serves as the strategic oversight body for the enterprise. The Board works closely with institutional leadership to establish strategic priorities, oversee enterprise planning and performance, ensure organizational sustainability, and advance Johns Hopkins Medicine's position as one of the world’s preeminent academic medical centers.

Specific Duties & Responsibilities

Governance & Board Affairs.

Serve as the principal advisor on board organizational matters for the JHM Board of Trustees.
Partner with the Dean/CEO, Board Chair/Co-Chairs, JHU and JHHS Secretaries, and Vice President/Chief of Staff to develop Board and Committee agendas, identify strategic issues requiring Board engagement, and support effective decision-making.
Provide support for the JHU President on JHM Executive Committee meetings.
Anticipate emerging issues and opportunities for Board consideration.
Monitor and recommend Board best practices and emerging trends affecting board operations.
Oversee and be primarily responsible for the development of minutes, committee charters, policies, resolutions, and related board records.
With JHU and JHHS Board Offices, coordinate board and committee self-assessments, trustee orientation, and continuing education.
Work with JHU and JHHS Board Offices and Development and Alumni Relations on trustee succession planning, as well as with Leadership Fellows on board composition initiatives.
Partner and collaborate closely with JHU and JHHS Board Offices to ensure alignment across the Johns Hopkins enterprise.
Develop and maintain trusted working relationships with the Chair/Co-Chairs of the JHM Board and other trustees, as well as liaise with institutional leadership, faculty, staff, and external entities related to the work of the JHM Board Office.
With support from Executive Speech Writer, prepare talking points and briefing materials, including for the JHM CEO, in advance of Board meetings.

Board Operations & Engagement

Provide oversight and strategic direction for Board meetings, events, retreats, orientation programs, and trustee engagement activities.
Recommend best practices and process improvements in trustee engagement and Board activities.
Supervise Board Office staff responsible for logistics, event execution, board portals (Diligent), meeting support, and administrative operations.
Ensure delivery of exceptional trustee experiences and service.

Strategic Initiatives

Lead or support special projects and ad hoc strategic initiatives as delegated by the Vice President/Chief of Staff.
Provide strategic planning and operational support to the Vice President/Chief of Staff on JHM priorities.
Develop and manage implementation plans on select initiatives and ensure effective coordination, communication, and execution.
Develop recommendations, briefing materials, and presentations to support executive decision-making and strategic planning efforts.
Partner with the Vice President/Chief of Staff to plan and facilitate key executive leadership meetings and forums, including development of agendas, briefing materials, action tracking, and follow-up on strategic decisions.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree.
Seven years of progressively responsible professional experience in board governance, executive administration, governance law, higher education administration, healthcare administration, or a related field.
Strategic project management experience.
Experience preparing executive-level correspondence, briefing materials, and presentations.
Additional education may substitute for required experience, and additional related experience may substitute for required education beyond a high school diploma/graduation equivalent, to the extent permitted by the JHU equivalency formula.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s Degree or Juris Doctor Degree.
Experience supporting governing boards, trustees, executives, or directors in a complex academic, healthcare, nonprofit, or corporate environment.

Technical Qualifications

High level of proficiency with Microsoft suite of products, including Word, Share Point, PowerPoint, and Excel, and Teams.
Experience using Diligent or comparable board management software.
